title: Boolean Algebra
body:
[[Complete Set of Operations]]

The algebra of two values, and the language [[Digital circuit]]s are designed in. Variables
are 0 or 1, and the operations are AND ($\cdot$), OR ($+$), and NOT ($\bar{x}$), each one
matching a gate.

The identities that do the work when simplifying a circuit:

| | |
|---|---|
| Identity | $x + 0 = x$, $x \cdot 1 = x$ |
| Null | $x + 1 = 1$, $x \cdot 0 = 0$ |
| Idempotent | $x + x = x$, $x \cdot x = x$ |
| Complement | $x + \bar{x} = 1$, $x \cdot \bar{x} = 0$ |
| Absorption | $x + xy = x$ |
| **De Morgan** | $\overline{x + y} = \bar{x}\bar{y}$, $\overline{xy} = \bar{x} + \bar{y}$ |

De Morgan's laws are the ones to actually memorise: they let you push a negation through
an expression, which is how any circuit gets converted into NAND-only form. That
conversion matters because `{NAND}` is a [[Complete Set of Operations]].

Fewer terms means fewer gates, so minimising a boolean expression is a hardware cost
saving, not just tidiness. [[Karnaugh Maps]] are the graphical way to do it.

This is propositional logic in a different notation: AND is $\land$, OR is $\lor$, NOT is
$\lnot$, and a truth table is a K-map without the Gray code. [[Systems of Logic]] in
[[THE NEW TURING OMNIBUS]] is the same structure written as a formal system, and it is where
the ladder up to predicate logic and [[Godel's Theorem]] starts.
